title: Beef Wellington
subtitle: Fillet of beef wrapped in mushroom duxelles and puff pastry
excerpt: A whole fillet of beef coated in a savoury mushroom paste, wrapped in puff pastry, and baked until the pastry is crisp and deeply golden and the beef inside is rosy pink. The great British celebration dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef Wellington is a British dish that came to prominence in the 1960s and 1970s, named (at least in popular culture) after the Duke of Wellington, though the connection is not documented. The dish consists of a whole beef fillet coated in a mushroom duxelles (a dry-cooked mushroom paste), sometimes with a thin layer of pate, wrapped in puff pastry and baked. The challenge of the dish is achieving a crisp, dry pastry base while keeping the beef pink inside: the mushroom layer acts as a moisture barrier, and resting the assembled Wellington in the fridge before baking helps set everything. A meat thermometer is necessary for accuracy: the centre should reach 50 to 52 C for rare, 54 to 56 C for medium-rare. The Wellington should rest for 10 minutes before slicing. It is among the most theatrical of all British main courses.

recipeTools.notes: A baking tray lined with baking parchment.
A large frying pan for searing the beef and cooking the mushrooms.

content.text: The mushroom duxelles must be cooked completely dry: any residual moisture will make the pastry soggy. Cook the mushrooms over high heat, stirring constantly, until they are a dark paste and all liquid has evaporated. This takes longer than expected, usually 12 to 15 minutes. The beef must be seared hard and then chilled before wrapping: warm beef steams the pastry. Assemble, refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, then bake directly from cold.

content.text: Season the beef all over with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over very high heat. Sear the beef for 2 minutes on each side until deeply browned all over. Brush with Dijon mustard while still hot. Leave to cool completely, then refrigerate.

Make the duxelles: cook the shallots in butter over medium heat for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme. Add the blended mushrooms and increase the heat to high. Cook, stirring constantly, for 12 to 15 minutes until the mushrooms are a dark, dry paste with no liquid remaining. Season well and cool completely.

Lay a sheet of cling film on the work surface. Spread the duxelles in a rectangle roughly the length and circumference of the beef. Place the beef at one edge and roll tightly, using the cling film to press the mushrooms firmly around the beef. Twist the ends to compress into a tight cylinder. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Unwrap the beef onto the pastry. Roll the pastry around the beef, sealing the join underneath and the ends tightly. Place seam-side down on a lined baking tray. Brush all over with egg wash and score lightly with a knife. Refrigerate for 15 minutes. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing thickly.
